newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine plans sell foreigners 26 pct alumina plant.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans sell foreigners 26 pct alumina plant.

text.p: Ukraine's state privatisation agency plans to sell 26 percent of shares in the country's sole alumina plant to a foreign strategic investor, the company's director said on Tuesday.
Vitaly Meshyn told reporters that the State Property Fund (FDM) proposal for privatising the Mykolaivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ) would require government approval.
The company, which has forecast output at 1.0 million tonnes this year, is one of 208 firms that Ukraine plans to put out for strategic investment tender.
Meshyn has been pushing to give employees a controlling stake in the plant, which exports 90 percent of its output to Russia.

A government commission awarded the workers' collective 30.97 percent of the shares after the country's highest court in August denied the collective the right to own a 40.14 percent stake in the plant.
The Fund has given the workers the right to purchase an additional 11.11 percent of shares, which would become available for foreign investment if workers did not buy them.
Under a plan which MHZ has agreed with the Fund, 25.1 percent of shares would remain in government hands, and about six percent would be auctioned off for privatisation certificates.
